title: How big would the tree be?
hints: The tree size of a `Num` is 1, and of an `Add` it is 1 plus the tree sizes of both children. Written as plain recursion, that is right but walks every path: `chain(60)` never finishes.
Keep a memo dict of the answers you've worked out, created inside `tree_size`, keyed by `id(node)`.
Don't key the dict on the node itself: these are frozen dataclasses, so hashing one hashes its fields, all the way down, as a tree. `id` is one small number.
prompt:
Write tree_size(e): how many nodes e would have if it were written out as a tree, with no sharing. That's also the number of calls the naive walk makes. tree_size(chain(3)) is 15, and tree_size(chain(60)) must finish.

The tree size of a node is 1 plus the tree sizes of its children. Write each node's answer down in a dict keyed by id(node).

answer.explain: Each distinct node is worked out once and then found in the memo by `id`, so `chain(60)` takes 61 computations instead of 2^61. Keying on the node itself would use the dataclass's structural hash, which walks the whole tree on every lookup. Python's ints never overflow, so even `chain(200)` gives the exact 2^201 - 1.
